belief: I should live in constant fear of the end times.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you should live in constant fear of the end times, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Frightening movies, books, or sermons about the end of the world. Childhood fear of being left behind. News of wars, disasters, and unrest. Teaching that focused on terror rather than hope. An anxious temperament that fixes on worst-case scenarios.
teaches: Jesus spoke honestly about hard days ahead, but He told His followers, “See to it that you are not alarmed.” He said that when these things happen, believers should lift up their heads, because their redemption is drawing near. God has not given us a spirit of fear but of power, love, and self-control. For believers, Christ’s return is called “the blessed hope.” The end of the story is Jesus making all things new.
self_statements: The end of the world terrifies me.
Every news story makes me panic.
I can’t enjoy life because the end might come.
I should be afraid if I’m taking this seriously.
Something terrible is about to happen.
I can’t stop thinking about the end times.
errors: Focusing on judgment while overlooking the blessed hope.
Predicting disaster for yourself without basis.
questions: What did Jesus say about being alarmed?
What should believers do when these things begin, according to Luke 21:28?
What kind of spirit has God given me?
Why does Scripture call Christ’s return “the blessed hope”?
Is the content I consume increasing fear or faith?
What would living with hope look like today?
truth: I do not have to live in constant fear of the end times. Jesus told me not to be alarmed. God has given me a spirit of power, love, and self-control. For believers, Christ’s return is the blessed hope, and the end of the story is Jesus making all things new. I can lift up my head with hope.
hw_questions: What did Jesus say about being alarmed?
What should I do when these things happen?
What spirit has God given me?
Why is Christ’s return a blessed hope?
Is my media increasing fear or faith?
hw_truths: Jesus told me not to be alarmed.
God has not given me a spirit of fear.
Christ’s return is my blessed hope.
I can lift up my head; my redemption is near.
The end of the story is Jesus making all things new.
log: Each day, write one reason the return of Jesus gives me hope.
name_example: For God has not given Sarah a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
actions: Limit end-times videos, news, or articles
for one week, and notice your anxiety level.
and write what the very end looks like.
When fear rises, read Luke 21:28 aloud
and take one useful step in your day.
Talk with a pastor or counselor
if end-times fear is affecting your sleep or daily life.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that Your return is my blessed hope. Help me reject the lie that I should live in constant fear of the end times. Give me Your peace, a spirit of power, love, and self-control, and help me lift up my head with hope. In Your name, Amen.
